summary: ITERATION 5 — Full backend + frontend verification of new Friend System, post/profile visibility, notifications, search, hard-delete cascade & regressions. BACKEND: 23/23 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_friends_system.py (junit at /app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_iteration5.xml). Covered: (1) A->B friend-request returns {status:outgoing,request_id}; B GET /friends/requests lists A; B GET /notifications has friend_request from A w/ correct request_id & read:false; /notifications/unread_count == 1; B accept -> friends bidirectional (A GET /friends contains B, A gets friend_accept notif, and B's originating friend_request notif flipped to read:true). (2) Decline path A->C then C declines: request row deleted, not in /friends/requests, friend_status returns 'none', and the originating notif is marked read. (3) Reverse auto-accept: after A->B outgoing, B->A auto-accepts and both /friends lists include each other. (4) DELETE /friends/{uid} truly unfriends (both users, both directions). (5) Cannot request self => 400. (6) /notifications/read zeroes unread_count. POST VISIBILITY: A creates public/friends/private posts; friend B reads friends 200, non-friend C 403, private 200 only for author, others 403; public readable by everyone; scope=friends returns A's public+friends (NOT private); scope=public returns only public posts from public-profile users (all items have visibility=public). PROFILE VISIBILITY: PUT /api/users/me privacy.profile_visibility=friends → friend B 200 with is_friend:true, non-friend C 403. private → both 403. public → all 200, sync-check confirms priv.profile_public==(vis=='public') on every flip, AND public feed for outside user contains the post while switching back to private removes it from the public feed (verified in same test). SEARCH: /api/users/search?q=Zorak<tag> returns tagged users, excludes self, INCLUDES private-profile user, each item carries is_friend + visibility. HARD DELETE CASCADE: A hard-deletes self; B's /friends list no longer contains A and B's /notifications contains no notif with actor.id==A (line 391-393 server.py wipes friendships and notifications). REGRESSION: /api/explore (comment moderation) still 200; POST/PUT/DELETE comment cycle still 200. FRONTEND: mobile (390x844) UI walked A-account via /(auth)/login. Feed screen: testIDs feed-scope, feed-notif-btn (badge shows '1' as expected because B sent friend req), feed-new-post all present. Compose modal renders 3-way Segmented with testID post-visibility (options Public/Friends/Private) plus post-text & post-submit. Notifications screen shows the pending request card with both testID='accept-{rid}' and testID='decline-{rid}' — clicking accept transitioned A↔B to friends (verified by /api/friends). Public profile /profile/{B_id}: because B is still on default (profile_visibility=private aka profile_public=false), server returned 403 as designed; UI shows testID='pp-private' EmptyState AND the friend-action button (testID='pp-unfriend' now that they are friends), exactly matching the requirement 'friends-only/private profiles still show the Add-friend button on the private screen'. Settings/profile tab: 3-way testID='privacy-visibility' segmented rendered. No red-screen errors; only benign React-Native-web console warnings (Unknown event handler property onResponderMove/Terminate/etc — noise from RN-Web pointer bridge, not a real bug).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1443-1453 are_friends/friend_ids — correct symmetric query on friendships with status:'accepted' and $or over requester/addressee. friend_ids maps the pair reciprocally. Good.

server.py:1675-1698 send_friend_request — validates target exists & is not self (400/404), returns {status:'friends'} if already friends (idempotent), REVERSE auto-accept path when the addressee re-requests the requester works (line 1689-1692 flips to accepted and creates a friend_accept notif for the original requester). One tiny observation: the reverse path only creates a notif for the ORIGINAL requester (body.user_id) but NOT for the person who triggered it — this is fine since they got the 'friends' response synchronously. Not a bug.

server.py:1701-1720 accept_friend/decline_friend — both correctly gated behind 'addressee==me' + pending, and BOTH mark {request_id:fid} notifications read via update_many, satisfying 'accepting/declining marks the originating notification read'. Verified end-to-end.

server.py:391-393 hard-delete purge — deletes friendships (both sides) AND notifications where user_id OR actor_id == uid. Confirmed downstream: after A self-deletes, B's notifications have zero entries with actor.id==A.

server.py:1613-1626 /users/search — regex on name (case-insensitive), excludes self via id:{$ne}, does NOT filter by privacy so ALL users are findable by name (matches PRD: 'requests can be sent to ALL users incl. private'), and returns is_friend + visibility fields.

server.py:1487-1494 /feed — scope=friends uses friend_ids + visibility {$in:[public,friends]}; scope=public restricts to authors with privacy.profile_public==true AND visibility=='public'. Matches spec.
server.py:413-419 profile_visibility sync — writing 'public'|'friends'|'private' keeps profile_public in sync (True iff visibility=='public'). Verified via PUT then GET /auth/me.
server.py:1518-1535 GET /posts/{pid} — enforces private/friends visibility. Private returns 403 for non-authors; friends returns 403 for non-friends. Author always sees own post.

server.py:1629-1653 /users/{uid}/profile — is_friend/relationship fields correctly returned; friends bypass 'friends-only' vis but NOT strictly 'private' (matches PRD wording 'friends bypass friends-only profiles').
frontend feed.tsx line 63: unread badge caps at '9+' — proper.
frontend notifications.tsx: useEffect POSTs /notifications/read on mount then invalidates notif-unread — good UX (bell badge clears when user opens the screen).
frontend profile/[id].tsx line 56-60: even in the 403 (private) branch it still renders the FriendButton (except when rel==='self'), which is the requested behavior.
seed_data_creation: All test users were ephemeral (test_<slug>_<uuid>@example.com), created via /api/auth/register and purged in teardown_class via DELETE /users/me. One extra pair (A/B) was created during the frontend automation and cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview backend is behind Cloudflare and rejects requests without a browser User-Agent (returns HTTP 403 'error code: 1010' when urllib default UA is used). If writing standalone httpclient tests, set User-Agent to any Mozilla-style string, OR use the requests library (its default UA passes). pytest suite uses `requests` and works fine. Login rate_limit is 10 attempts/60s per email in an in-memory dict — DO NOT run this suite via xdist with per-worker duplicate logins on the same email; each test class uses fresh users so parallelism at class-scope is safe, but we ran with `-n 0` (per project convention). Frontend web preview uses AsyncStorage which on web is backed by IndexedDB, so you cannot inject a token via localStorage — always log in through the actual /(auth)/login screen with testIDs login-email/login-password/login-submit.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found; all 23 backend tests + all 5 scoped frontend flows behave exactly per PRD.
